title: Scarred discrete time crystal in a periodically driven dimerized spin chain
authors: Davood Marripour, Saeed S. Jahromi, Jahanfar Abouie
abstract: We investigate the emergence of a scarred discrete time crystal (SDTC) phase in a periodically driven dimerized spin chain. While generic interacting Floquet systems are expected to thermalize according to the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH), we demonstrate that this system hosts quantum many-body scars (QMBS) that induce a regime of weak ergodicity breaking. Through an analysis of Floquet level statistics, entanglement entropy, and eigenstate fidelity, we identify a manifold of low-entanglement states characterized by semi-Poisson statistics embedded within an otherwise thermal spectrum. These scarred states support robust subharmonic oscillations with period doubling, signaling the spontaneous breaking of discrete time-translation symmetry. We show that the SDTC response is robust against a variety of initial state configurations, demonstrating its stability beyond fine-tuned conditions. A finite-size scaling analysis reveals that the time-crystalline lifetime grows with system size within the range accessible to our exact-diagonalization calculations. However, drawing on the general phenomenology of approximate many-body scars, we expect that hybridization between Floquet scars and the thermal continuum will eventually curtail this growth, causing the lifetime to saturate at system sizes beyond our current numerical reach. This characterizes the SDTC as a long-lived metastable dynamical regime rather than a strictly stable thermodynamic phase, providing a comprehensive framework for understanding the interplay between periodic driving and constrained many-body dynamics in disorder-free systems.
summary: The paper investigates Scarred Discrete Time Crystals (SDTCs) in a dimerized spin chain under periodic driving. It demonstrates that the system enters a weakly ergodic regime characterized by quantum many-body scars, evidenced by semi-Poisson level statistics and subharmonic oscillations. The authors conclude that this SDTC is a long-lived metastable state whose stability can be mapped against the onset of full thermalization.
main_problem: The study investigates the emergence of a Scarred Discrete Time Crystal (SDTC) phase in a periodically driven dimerized spin chain, specifically addressing how weak ergodicity breaking occurs relative to full thermalization.
main_result: The system exhibits QMBS leading to robust subharmonic oscillations, confirming SDTC behavior; this regime is characterized as a long-lived metastable dynamical state rather than a stable thermodynamic phase.
method: Analysis involves calculating Floquet level statistics (comparing semi-Poisson vs. Wigner-Dyson), measuring entanglement entropy, and performing finite-size scaling on the time-crystalline lifetime.
model_or_system: The model is a periodically driven antiferromagnetic dimerized spin chain governed by a two-step Floquet cycle ($U = e^{-i H_{dd}t_2}e^{-i H_d t_1}$). The Hamiltonian includes XY coupling within dimers and inter-dimer interactions ($\lambda, h, \Delta$).
key_observables: Semi-Poisson level statistics (signature of QMBS), subharmonic oscillations with period doubling (SDTC signature), Wigner-Dyson statistics (thermal limit), and time-crystalline lifetime.
important_parameters: The primary control parameters are the dimer coupling ($J$), inter-dimer interaction ($\lambda$), and magnetic fields ($h, \Delta$). The crossover is driven by varying $	ilde{J}$ relative to a critical value.
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on the zero-magnetization sector and treats the SDTC as a long-lived metastable regime whose lifetime is expected to saturate due to hybridization with the thermal continuum at large sizes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the crossover of spectral statistics from semi-Poisson (small $	ilde{J}$, scarred) towards Wigner-Dyson (large $	ilde{J}$, thermalized), and show finite-size scaling confirming this transition flow.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model, details diagnostic tools like level spacing analysis, presents results mapping the crossover between non-ergodic/scarred dynamics and ergodic/thermal dynamics, and concludes by framing the SDTC as a metastable phenomenon.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical framework for understanding how structured quantum dynamics (scars) can resist thermalization in clean, periodically driven systems, which is highly relevant to Floquet engineering applications in AMO physics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Schematic representation of the periodically driven dimerized spin chain. The driving cycle T = t1 + t2 consists of two distinct phases: during t1, the dimers evolve as non- interacting units, while during t2, a dimer-dimer interaction and an external magnetic field are introduced.

FIG. 3: Level spacing distribution P(s) for system sizes L = 14, 16, and 18 in the weakly non-ergodic regime. Here, ˜∆= 0.11, ˜J = 0.15, ˜h = 1 and λt2 = 0.9. The green dash-dotted and red dashed curves denote the analytical predictions for semi-Poisson and WD statistics, respectively. The observed finite-size flow indicates that as L increases, the numerical data systematically depart from the semi-Poissonian regime toward the WD distribution, signaling an eventual crossover to thermalization in the thermodynamic limit.

FIG. 2: (Top): Level spacing distribution P(s) obtained from the aggregated symmetry sectors. The resulting Pois- sonian statistics highlight the necessity of partitioning the global U(1) symmetry to avoid spurious non-ergodic signa- tures. (Bottom): Level spacing distribution P(s) for the driven dimer chain with ˜∆= 0.11, ˜J = 0.15, ˜h = 1 and λt2 = 0.9, and L = 16. The numerical results in the { ˜J, ˜∆} < 1 regime exhibit semi-Poisson statistics, signal- ing constrained dynamics and many-body scars. Theoretical Poisson and WD distributions are shown for comparison.

FIG. 4: Level spacing distribution P(s) for the periodically driven chain of length L = 16, with ˜∆= 0.11, ˜h = 1 and λt2 = 0.9, evaluated at the larger coupling ˜J = 0.7. At this value of ˜J the statistics shift from the semi-Poissonian regime toward the WD distribution, indicating a transition into the fully ergodic thermal phase.

FIG. 6: Average level-spacing ratio ⟨r⟩versus the coupling ˜J for system sizes L = 12, 14, and 16, with ˜∆= 0.11 and λt2 = 0.9. The black and red dashed lines denote the theoretical Poisson (≈0.39) and WD (≈0.53) limits, respectively. The increasing sharpness of the crossover with L is a signature of the transition from the constrained regime to a fully ergodic thermal phase.
